title: Immune Rejuvenation-Associated Protein Signals and Circulating Microenvironment Remodeling Following Oral Procyanidin C1 Supplementation: A Retrospective Longitudinal Study
content: Recent cell and animal studies have suggested that procyanidin C1 (PCC1) has potential for targeting senescent cells, but its eﬀects in humans remain unclear. This retrospective study analyzed existing records from 32 participants aged 46–78 years during four rounds of oral supplementation with a PCC1-containing supplement. We assembled results for more than 100 circulating proteins in plasma before supplementation,after the ﬁrst round and after all four rounds. We used multiple protein-based approaches to jointly assess age-associated and immune-health-associated features. Six primary directional scores were constructed from published evidence: a 12-protein combination with concordant age associations across studies, a 19-protein combination based on age associations in healthy populations, the OrganAge local score (97 proteins), the ipfP3GPT local score (77 proteins), the 58-protein core immune age-direction score, and the 19-protein Immune Health Metric (IHM)-associated protein-direction score. The data showed that multiple chemokines and soluble receptors were below baseline in most participants after four rounds of LB-150 supplementation.A small number of protein factors nevertheless remained above baseline. For individual markers within this subset, subsequent follow-up showed group-level values close to baseline, while changes at later time points remain to be observed. Across the six primary protein scores, both median scores and most participants'scores indicated shifts toward protein paterns associated with younger age or beter immune health in the higher and lower cumulative-intake groups. Relative to baseline, the group medians of the 58-protein core immune age-direction score and the 19-protein IHM-associated protein-direction score indicated older-age-associated and poorer-immune-health-associated features, respectively, after the ﬁrst round. After all four rounds, the corresponding medians indicated features associated with younger age and beter immune health. This patern of group medians was observed under both cumulative-intake regimens and in the age subgroups within the higher cumulative-intake group. By examining protein-age associations and immune-health-associated features, this study identiﬁed human protein changes after oral intake of a PCC1-containing supplement. The ﬁndings suggest immunomodulatory potential for PCC1 and provide human observations that connect with existing senescent-cell research and inform further investigation of immune health and modulation of the circulating immune microenvironment.
